correctness.rationale: For every generic fixed-offset hyperplane, each j-face of a simplex section is a mixed-sign (j+2)-vertex simplex face, giving the exact binomial polynomial. A centered isotropic Gaussian direction gives K_n(t)=#{G_i>Gbar+sqrt(n)t s_n}. Uniform local empirical-cdf control at random O_p(n^-1/2) thresholds, the expansions of Gbar and sample s_n, and Lindeberg give the influence function psi_c and variance v(c). The polynomial second derivative at balance yields the rank-one noncentral square at n t->h. First derivatives yield Gaussian laws for n t->infinity with sqrt(n)t->0 and for t=c/sqrt(n), all jointly across fixed ranks. Exact small-n face enumerations, 3,600-seed ensemble checks and asymptotic coefficient checks replay successfully from verify.py. Finite tests do not prove weak convergence. No result is asserted for growing ranks.

value.rationale: The offset is a natural geometric parameter for slicing a canonical convex body. A singular, non-Gaussian central face-vector fluctuation law was known, but the fate of that law off the centroid was not addressed by the closest checked sources. The result identifies a sharp physical distance scale 1/n, the entire noncentral crossover family, a distinct intermediate Gaussian normalization, and a fixed-scale Gaussian law with a nontrivial sample-normalizer correction. All fixed face ranks fluctuate through the same random factor, making the conclusion structural rather than a finite special-case count. It supplies a natural comparative benchmark for random section complexity without claiming a general arbitrary-polytope theorem.
